articles.title_orig: New satellite data shows how fast some African cities are sinking
articles.title_zh: New satellite data shows how fast some African cities are sinking
articles.content_orig:
Some of Africa's largest cities are sinking faster than previously thought, new research shows.
Scientists used radar imagery from the European Space Agency's Sentinel-1 satellites to map how much the land beneath 20 African coastal cities had moved.
The study found that some cities - including Lagos in Nigeria and Alexandria in Egypt - were sinking much faster than previously estimated in 2021 by the UN's climate body, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).
While some causes of this sinking, or subsidence, are natural, many are the result of human activities, such as the extraction of groundwater from underneath the Earth's surface.
Lead author Oluwaseyi Dasho said the effects of subsidence "are often invisible in everyday life, but over decades they can substantially increase flood exposure".
This is because when the ground sinks it becomes lower relative to the ocean and adds to the risk of the sea level rises caused by climate change .
Seven million people, one billion buildings and $180bn (£137bn) of assets could be at flood risk by 2050, the paper estimated.
In the past, a lack of monitoring stations has prevented scientists from obtaining up-to-date localised information on subsidence in Africa, Dasho said.
But by using satellite data, the researchers from Virginia Tech were able to detect land movements as small as 1mm per year.
Senior author Manoochehr Shirzaei said Sentinel-1 satellites flew over the same region of the Earth every six to 12 days.
"[The satellite] transmits the radar signal, which hits the ground and bounces back to the satellite," the geosciences professor explained. This process is then repeated on "many revisits".
The time between sending the signal and receiving it back is recorded, with changes in this value over time revealing how much the land has moved.
The ground under Alexandria and Lagos was found to have sunk an average of 6mm and 5mm per year respectively.
If this rate continued, sea levels around Alexandria would rise 36% more by 2050 than the IPCC predicted , under the middle estimates for how much planet-warming emissions will increase.
Luanda in Angola has also sunk significantly, but other cities such as Durban in South Africa have remained stable or even risen slightly.
Shirzaei said showing where the IPCC had underestimated risks - but also where the threat had been overestimated - could help planners allocate resources more effectively.
The man-made drivers of subsidence are usually "extremely local, [which] means that we can combat them by creating local policies", Shirzaei explained.
One major cause is the increased water consumption of rapidly growing cities. Too much water being extracted from the ground can lead to the soil becoming compacted and the surface sinking.
The Aswan Dam on the Nile may also be trapping sediment upstream and preventing the replacement of sinking land in Alexandria, the study suggests.
In Lagos, the reclaiming of land from the ocean to create artificial islands and the construction of buildings on loose ground are other possible causes of subsidence.
Methods of preventing cities from sinking include supplying other water sources and growing less water-intensive crops.
"Whatever we cannot mitigate, we try to adapt to it," Shirzaei added. This could mean building flood defences or moving key infrastructure to a higher level .
The professor said developing countries had been "left out" of much of the planning for sea-level rises due to a lack of monitoring.
The techniques developed in this study could potentially be used to address the knowledge gap in other regions, such as the Pacific islands, Shirzaei suggested.
Oluwaseyi Dasho said he hoped the paper, in Science Advances, could help African governments "prepare adequately for future challenges and more importantly for the future generations".

articles.title_orig: Gold and Silver Jump as Beijing Vows to Support China's Stock Market
articles.title_zh: Gold and Silver Jump as Beijing Vows to Support China's Stock Market
articles.content_orig:
Chinese stocks rebounded sharply on Friday after a rare intraday state media readout cheered investors as top policymakers pledged to expand the role of state-backed funds in supporting the market.
The STAR index surged 14%, led by Chinese chipmakers such as CXMT , Cambricon and SMIC. The CSI Semiconductor index of 40 chip stocks climbed by 17.6% in its biggest single-day gain on record, surpassing the prior record of nearly 17% in late 2024, according to Wind Information.
The gains were widespread across mainland and Hong Kong stock indexes. The Hang Seng index rose 2%, while the CSI 300 index climbed 4%, its biggest jump since October 2024, according to Wind data.
The rally comes as governments pour support into domestic chip industries while tightening controls on sensitive technology in the global race for artificial intelligence.
The U.S. unveiled a new rule last week to further restrict Chinese companies’ access to advanced AI chips, including through overseas data centers, adding pressure on Beijing to accelerate its push for semiconductor self-sufficiency.
Friday's rally comes after the CSI 300 on Thursday sank to its lowest level since the escalation of the U.S.-China tariff war in the spring of 2025, according to Wind data.
In recent months, investors have weighed the commercial feasibility of Chinese artificial intelligence developers and tighter U.S. restrictions on advanced chips.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang oversaw a meeting Friday morning of the State Council, the country's top governing body, which saw officials pledge to strengthen the role of "National Team" — referring to state-backed funds — to stabilize markets and ensure ample liquidity, according to a readout released by state media Xinhua News.
The explicit reference to the "national team" is a first for a State Council meeting, said Bob Chen, a Shanghai-based venture capitalist and economist.
Authorities also stressed that "capital markets are crucial to the broader economy," according to the readout, a rare comment from a government that has not always looked favorably on the financial sector.
"Stock market performance is now prioritized at the highest level for the Chinese government," which is boosting investor confidence, Chen said.
"That's very strong language from the top officials," said Zong Ke, a portfolio manager at a Shanghai-based quantitative fund.
By Ke's calculations, stock trading volumes surged rapidly after the readout was released around 1:00 p.m. local time (12:00 a.m. ET). Full-day turnover across the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges was 52% higher than the previous session.
Policymakers also vowed to strengthen the role of "stabilization funds" like Central Huijin Investment, a state-owned investment firm that holds equity stakes on behalf of the State Council.
That message "effectively institutionalized Central Huijin's role as a state stabilization fund," said Hong Hao, managing partner of Lotus Asset Management. "And it's significantly positive news for the market."
Hao expects this market rally to prove more durable than the "fleeting bounce" triggered by Beijing's stimulus talks in the past, which wore off in days. "This time it's for real."
The readout of the Cabinet's meeting, typically released well after trading hours, was published around noon local time during trading hours, an unusual timing that's viewed by markets as a bullish signal.
The State Council also pledged better policies to steer medium- or long-term funds, such as insurance and social security funds, into equities, and encouraged listed companies to pay more dividends and step up share buybacks, while vowing a crackdown on financial fraud to protect investors.
The national team will accelerate asset purchases, Ke said, adding that he expects more supportive policies to follow, such as further loosening the institutional constraints that have limited long-term funds from investing in stocks.
Beijing's reliance on intervention to offset stock volatility has, however, raised questions about the market's ability to sustain longer-term gains.
But the market needs this kind of support right now, said Ke, as the near-term aim is to ease liquidity pressure and restore confidence so the market doesn't fall much further.
Chinese AI-related stocks also carry less downside risk than their U.S. counterparts, as the companies have spent less on AI so far and their shares have already been through a sharp correction, Ke said.
That, together with the pledged state backing, has given investors more confidence that the market may be nearing its bottom, Ke added.

Dutch authorities ​seized 26 critically endangered mud turtles at Amsterdam ’s Schiphol airport last week, the Dutch Food and Consumer ⁠Product Safety Authority (NVWA) said on Friday.
The Vallarta turtles were brought in from Mexico, where a mere 300 of them are believed to remain in the wild.
Vallarta turtles are one of the world’s smallest turtle species, and have been linked with illegal trade due to their considerable financial value.
According to the NVWA, the turtles were hidden in the checked baggage of ​a ⁠man who was travelling ‌to Hong Kong .
The man was subsequently arrested, while further investigations are ongoing.
Most of the turtles were packed inside of a box alongside a toy car, while a handful of others were placed inside of a sealed sock.
The turtles had been wrapped in duct tape to prevent them from moving.
All of the turtles survived and were taken to a specialist animal rescue centre, the NVWA said.
According to the US-based ⁠ Center for Biological Diversity , Vallarta mud turtles are sold for large sums in China .
“Vallarta mud turtles sell for up to $30,000 each in China, providing a major financial incentive that drives illegal trade,” it said in a statement last month, calling on ‌the Mexican ​government to do ‌more to protect the ​animals.
“Experts believe wildlife authorities only seize a small portion of illegal traded wildlife.”
A similar incident occurred in December 2025 at Los Angeles International Airport , the Center said, where “approximately 20 Vallarta mud turtles bound for Asia” were seized.
Based on US Fish and Wildlife Service data, Tara Easter, a University of Michigan doctoral candidate who has studied the trade, previously estimated the commercial export trade for mud turtles in the United States increased from 1,844 in 1999 to nearly 40,000 in 2017.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia chips on sale for $3M in China — as Jensen Huang scandal and US crackdown chokes supply
articles.title_zh: Nvidia chips on sale for $3M in China — as Jensen Huang scandal and US crackdown chokes supply
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia is selling its most cutting-edge chips to at least two companies that are U.S.-based, but are actually controlled by Chinese-owned firms, raising fresh questions about efforts to keep sensitive technology away from the nation's rivals, a CBS News investigation found.
One of the chip giant's "preferred partners" is a California company owned by a Chinese firm whose chief executive is a graduate of a Chinese military university, records show. Another California company was renamed after its Chinese-owned parent company was blacklisted.
Some of these U.S.-based, Chinese-owned firms have then leased or sold the advanced chips, used for artificial intelligence, to other companies in Southeast Asia, records show.
The world of computer chip exports is murky — and labyrinthine chains of custody have made it even more difficult to determine just how many of the most sensitive Nvidia chips are being exploited by China, experts told CBS News.
"It is a wake-up call for accountability, for properly resourcing the enforcement bodies, and for every leading private-sector tech company to map where it is exposed," said Mishel Kondi, a senior analyst at C4ADS, which specializes in using public data, from corporate filings to satellite imagery, to uncover sanctions violations and smuggling.
C4ADS, a Washington-based global security nonprofit also known as the Center for Advanced Defense Studies, examined corporate filings and other company ownership data at the request of CBS News. This story is based on dozens of corporate filings, court records and an investigation of Nvidia's corporate relationships dating back to 2023 — long before its CEO Jensen Huang and his behemoth chip company dominated the news cycle.
That explosive saga began 27 days ago when the news broke that Huang had been having an affair with Alice Huang — a woman whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The Justice Department has said it has not reached a conclusion, and Beijing denies she is a spy. The company she ran, Megaspeed, a cloud computing company based in Singapore, is under investigation by the Justice Department for allegedly circumventing export bans by obtaining computer chips for use by China.
But Megaspeed , national security and trade experts say, is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the transfer of Nvidia chips to China. And elected officials are now asking questions like: How are Nvidia's chips getting to China? And what did Jensen Huang and his colleagues know about it?
"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a senior Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement this week.
Nvidia had almost $20 billion in sales to China last year. The company can sell graphics cards for personal computers and server chips with lower processing power to China without a special license.
What is not allowed — and is under strict export controls — are the sales of Nvidia's most technologically advanced chips, which are powering the AI revolution.
But recent reporting, including from CBS News, has shown some of the highest end chips, called Blackwells, have made it into Chinese hands.
The circuitous trail traveled by Nvidia chips quickly gets muddy.
Take RiCloud AI, a data center company based in San Jose, California. RiCloud AI appears on Nvidia's list of "preferred partners" in the U.S., affording it preferential access to sales of high-end computer chips used for advanced AI models.
These are classified as American sales, according to Nvidia's public filings — with the chips going to RiCloud AI, Inc., a U.S. company.
But RiCloud AI's parent company is Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Limited. That company is headquartered in Shenzhen, China, and is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange.
Yuxing's CEO and co-owner, Cong Yu, has a degree in National Defense Mobilization from the People's Liberation Army Command College, a university run by the Chinese military. Yu is also CEO of a related RiCloud company in California.
And Yuxing's chairman, Li Qiang, was previously chairman of data firm Global Switch Holdings, which was dropped as a data center provider by Australia's Department of Defense in June 2024 over national security concerns.
The U.S. government has not accused RiCloud and Yuxing of any wrongdoing.
By December 2025, just 10 weeks after it was incorporated, RiCloud AI had secured its partner status with Nvidia and has since become a "preferred" cloud partner, giving the company priority access to advanced chips, Nvidia's software and technical support. Nvidia has not responded to questions about what background checks it conducted before awarding the privileged status to RiCloud AI.
An examination of RiCloud AI's clients suggests that some seem like unorthodox customers for such high-powered technology. This year, for example, it signed a $120 million deal to lease 300 Nvidia B300 servers to a company in Taiwan that was primarily known for selling whisky.
Agencia Comercial Spirits was a small whisky importer with $609,000 in net income in 2025 when it listed on the Nasdaq as an AI company. This year it has made commitments for AI data center-related deals totaling between $488 and $598 million, after Li was appointed as chairman.
Agencia did not respond to a request for comment. In a February press release announcing its pivot into data centers, Agencia said the move was "part of a broader review of strategic opportunities outside its core whisky business."
Then there is California company Aivres, which is currently listed on Nvidia's website as an "elite" compute partner — the highest tier of relationship with the chip giant.
Aivres used to be called Inspur, the same name as its Chinese parent company. But when Inspur group firms in China were added to a federal blacklist of companies considered a security risk to the U.S. in March 2023, the California subsidiary changed its name and today still maintains its close relationship with Nvidia. Aivres itself is not on the blacklist.
Aivres, which produces data center servers housing Nvidia chips, exported at least $5.6 billion of advanced technology to Southeast Asia between April 2024 and February 2026, according to a New York Times analysis of trade records published two months ago.
Some $3 billion of those exports were for computers containing Nvidia's cutting-edge Blackwell chips, which are restricted from being exported to China, the Times reported.
The Aivres chips then went to two companies in Malaysia — Megaspeed and Aolani — providing cloud AI services to Chinese firms Alibaba and ByteDance, according to the Times.
Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm where Jensen Huang paramour Alice Huang was a top executive, was blacklisted by the U.S. government this week, in the wake of the scandal. The company denies any wrongdoing.
The Pentagon put Alibaba on a blacklist in June, claiming it used advanced chips to help the Chinese military. The company denies it and sued the government over the blacklisting, winning a preliminary injunction last month.
The servers owned by Inspur — Aivres' parent company — are used in China by the country's military, according to the U.S. government . Aivres did not respond to requests for comment.
Another of Nvidia's elite U.S. partners has surfaced in a recent $300 million chip smuggling case, though it has not been accused of wrongdoing.
Earlier this year, a California businessman named Greg Lui was indicted for allegedly smuggling export-controlled chips to China via Malaysia and Singapore in 2023 and 2024. He has pleaded not guilty.
Records reviewed by CBS News link Lui to 2CRSi, an Nvidia elite partner in the U.S. that is a branch of a French-owned company making AI data servers.

articles.title_orig: Kyiv offers Black Sea ceasefire to protect grain exports
articles.title_zh: Kyiv offers Black Sea ceasefire to protect grain exports
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine has presented a proposal for a possible ceasefire in the Black Sea, as Kyiv seeks to protect its grain exports amid escalating attacks on shipping and port infrastructure.
Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced the proposal on Friday during the “Food from Ukraine” conference, saying Kyiv was ready to restore freedom of navigation and ensure the uninterrupted export of agricultural products.
“We are now awaiting a response from Russia. All of our proposals have been conveyed,” Sybiha said.
Moscow has sought to include oil transportation in the proposed ceasefire deal, but the Ukrainians say that issue belongs in a broader energy ceasefire.
He accused Russia of repeatedly putting forward “unrealistic demands” in response to Kyiv’s proposals, according to Suspilne, Ukraine’s national broadcaster.
The latest ceasefire initiative comes amid growing international concern over the security of commercial shipping and global food supplies. Ukraine and Russia are both major agricultural exporters , and attacks on vessels and port infrastructure have disrupted shipments transiting through the Black Sea.
A previous UN- and Turkiye-brokered agreement allowed Ukrainian grain exports to resume following Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022.
However, Moscow withdrew from the arrangement in July 2023, prompting Kyiv to establish an alternative maritime export corridor.
In August, Reuters reported that Ukraine had conveyed an earlier proposal through a third party for both sides to halt attacks on civilian targets in the Black Sea. At the time, Ukrainian grain exports had fallen 76 percent year-on-year, as shipowners avoided ports in the Odesa region following repeated Russian strikes.
International efforts to secure a limited ceasefire have since gained traction.
On October 31, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was reviewing proposals from Turkiye and India to facilitate uninterrupted grain and energy shipments.
The diplomatic impasse also comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy voiced his frustrations with US President Donald Trump’s approach to Moscow.
In an interview with the BBC on Friday, Zelenskyy criticised Trump for describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” following their meeting in China last week.
“It’s strange. He is an aggressor and a killer. He can’t be a friend. Just cannot be,” Zelenskyy said.
He also criticised Washington for what he described as excessive neutrality in its dealings with Moscow, arguing that the US should use its influence to pressure Russia into meaningful negotiations.
“When you try to be very neutral with the aggressor … it means you support victims and you support also aggressor. It’s not right,” he said.
After talks in Florida on Wednesday, the NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called on Russia to avoid actions that could expand the war and urged a peaceful resolution as soon as possible.
Rutte has also stressed that any eventual peace agreement or long-term ceasefire must include security guarantees for Ukraine.

articles.content_orig:

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Financial commentator and stockbroker Peter Schiff took aim at Donald Trump 's trade policies Friday, calling him "the biggest loser of any president" as the U.S. goods trade deficit continues to widen despite the president’s aggressive tariffs .
Schiff's comments came after the goods trade deficit jumped 10.7 percent to $149.5 billion in October, according to the Census Bureau's latest advance report . For this year, imports totaled $365.3 billion, while exports came in at just $215.8 billion.
The gap was more than double what it was in October 2025.
“It was the third-largest monthly deficit in history, exceeded only by January and March of 2025, when importers rushed to avoid tariffs,” Schiff said. “On trade, Trump is the biggest loser of any president,” he wrote on X .
The deficit has also climbed steadily in recent months, rising from $118.9 billion in July.
The latest numbers come as Trump continues to defend his tariffs , which have been a major part of his economic agenda during his second term.
Trump previously pointed to a 55 percent drop in the trade deficit in April 2026 as a sign that his tariffs were working. He celebrated the numbers on Truth Social , writing , “THANK YOU MR. TARIFF !”
But the deficit has since climbed again, putting Trump's claims about the success of his trade policies under fresh scrutiny.
Trump has continued pushing new tariffs despite mounting political and legal challenges. On Wednesday, his administration announced proposed import taxes on goods from China, the European Union and 12 other trading partners.
The administration says the tariffs are meant to stop foreign countries from making too many goods and selling them cheaply, arguing that government subsidies and other trade practices give overseas companies an unfair advantage over U.S. manufacturers.
China could face tariffs of up to 20 percent , while the proposed rates for other trading partners range from 15 percent to 35 percent, depending on the country. The measures are not final, and the administration is accepting public comments before taking further action.
The latest proposals also come after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's sweeping 2025 tariffs earlier this year, forcing the administration to pursue a different legal path to impose import taxes.
Schiff, who serves as chief economist and global strategist at Euro Pacific Asset Management and hosts “The Peter Schiff Show,” an investing podcast, is no stranger to criticizing Trump's economic policies.
The stockbroker also clashed with Trump last year after appearing on Fox News. Trump later called Schiff a “Trump-hating loser who has already proven to be wrong.”

By Ke's calculations, stock trading volumes surged rapidly after the readout was released around 1:00 p.m. local time (12:00 a.m. ET). Full-day turnover across the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges was 52% higher than the previous session.
Policymakers also vowed to strengthen the role of "stabilization funds" like Central Huijin Investment, a state-owned investment firm that holds equity stakes on behalf of the State Council.
That message "effectively institutionalized Central Huijin's role as a state stabilization fund," said Hong Hao, managing partner of Lotus Asset Management. "And it's significantly positive news for the market."
Hao expects this market rally to prove more durable than the "fleeting bounce" triggered by Beijing's stimulus talks in the past, which wore off in days. "This time it's for real."
The readout of the Cabinet's meeting, typically released well after trading hours, was published around noon local time during trading hours, an unusual timing that's viewed by markets as a bullish signal.
The State Council also pledged better policies to steer medium- or long-term funds, such as insurance and social security funds, into equities, and encouraged listed companies to pay more dividends and step up share buybacks, while vowing a crackdown on financial fraud to protect investors.
The national team will accelerate asset purchases, Ke said, adding that he expects more supportive policies to follow, such as further loosening the institutional constraints that have limited long-term funds from investing in stocks.
Beijing's reliance on intervention to offset stock volatility has, however, raised questions about the market's ability to sustain longer-term gains.
But the market needs this kind of support right now, said Ke, as the near-term aim is to ease liquidity pressure and restore confidence so the market doesn't fall much further.
Chinese AI-related stocks also carry less downside risk than their U.S. counterparts, as the companies have spent less on AI so far and their shares have already been through a sharp correction, Ke said.
That, together with the pledged state backing, has given investors more confidence that the market may be nearing its bottom, Ke added.

articles.title_orig: NBC pulls ‘indefensible’ anti-Israel ad that aired during ‘SNL’ special: ‘Carefully orchestrated lie’
articles.title_zh: NBC pulls ‘indefensible’ anti-Israel ad that aired during ‘SNL’ special: ‘Carefully orchestrated lie’
articles.content_orig:
The 30-second spot claimed Israel uses U.S. military aid to target children
Roberto Machado Noa/LightRocket via Getty Images
NBC logo at Universal Studios.
NBC aired an ad on Wednesday during the Thanksgiving special of “Saturday Night Live” encouraging viewers to oppose U.S. aid to Israel, claiming Israel uses such aid to target Palestinian children.
The 30-second spot, which aired nationally and was paid for by the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project , depicted an American girl saving $400 for a new bike, before showing a girl in Gaza on crutches with one leg. A narrator says, “Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to Israel to do this.”
The ad directs viewers to IMEU Policy Project’s “No More for Israel” campaign site, which says, “The US government has sent Israel over $330 billion in inflation-adjusted dollars since 1948. That’s $400 every three seconds nonstop for nearly eighty years. Much of it with our tax dollars.”
The figure appears to be referencing high-end estimates of such assistance — the Congressional Research Service most recently estimated it was approximately $298 billion, inflation adjusted, between 1946 and 2024. It also obscures that almost all U.S. military assistance to Israel is now spent within the U.S and that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has championed ending U.S. aid to Israel, including President Donald Trump’s announcement earlier this month that he had agreed with Netanyahu to wind down assistance by the end of the year.
Jewish leaders immediately condemned the decision by NBC to air the ad. Ted Deutch, CEO of the American Jewish Committee, noted that the spot did not reference Hamas or its Oct. 7, 2023, massacre, and called on NBC to “explain why and how an ad this one-sided and manipulative met its standards for what it will put on the air.”
Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt said NBC’s decision to air the ad was “indefensible” and that there is “no rationale to justify fanning the flames” of rising antisemitism “with such a twisted narrative.”
William Daroff, CEO of the Conference of Presidents of Major American Jewish Organizations, called NBC’s airing of the spot a “shanda.”
The National Jewish Advocacy Center sent a letter to Mark Marshall, chairman of global advertising and partnerships at NBCUniversal, noting that NBC’s “own published standards required a factual basis for that claim before it reached the air” and requesting that the network provide such reasoning to the public.
The decision to air the ad was especially notable given that Brian Roberts, chairman and CEO of Comcast, NBCUniversal’s parent company, hails from a prominent Jewish family that has been publicly and financially supportive of Israel.
Following the Oct. 7 attacks, Roberts and Comcast President Mike Cavanagh sent a note to employees saying they were “horrified and deeply saddened by the brutal attack on Israel,” expressing solidarity with “the families who have lost their loved ones through unspeakable acts of terrorism and the devastation of war.” Comcast pledged $2 million to humanitarian aid efforts in Israel and around the region.
Daniel Lubetzky, the founder of KIND Snacks, focused his criticism on Semafor , the outlet which broke the story that IMEU Policy Project would be running the ad. He said the outlet “needs to be investigated for corruption. And for sure should not be treated as journalism,” following on his accusation last month that the outlet is compromising its journalistic independence through its financial ties to Qatar.
Deutch similarly called out Semafor for reporting on the ad “largely on the terms its sponsors wanted, with remarkably little scrutiny of what the ad leaves out.”

articles.title_orig: Earliest iron scale armor in China found near First Emperor’s tomb
articles.title_zh: Earliest iron scale armor in China found near First Emperor’s tomb
articles.content_orig:
Archaeologists working beside the mausoleum of China’s First Emperor have uncovered what appears to be the earliest complete suit of iron scale armor ever found in the country. A team from University College London and the Emperor Qin Shihuang’s Mausoleum Site Museum reported the find in the journal Antiquity.
The armor came from tomb M1, the third of nine large tombs stretching west of the emperor’s main burial enclosure. Crews excavated the site from 2013 to 2023. The main chamber covers 1,900 square meters and sits 15.6 meters below ground. Inside, the team found two coffins, a four-wheeled wooden carriage and horse-and-chariot burials in side pits. No other Qin tomb dug so far is richer or better preserved. Nobody knows who lay there, but the person held high rank.
The iron scales sat in a heap on the south side of the chamber. The ceiling collapsed long ago, and the scales likely dropped from a shelf. Corrosion broke most of the metal into tiny pieces, yet the team still counted at least 200 larger fragments. They estimate the suit held 800 to 1,200 scales. A helmet would need only 80 to 90, and several suits would need far more, so the pile points to one body piece. Such a garment would weigh about 10 kilograms.
Most scales are small rectangles, roughly 33 by 29 millimeters and 1.5 millimeters thick, with 10 tiny holes for lacing. A heavier type has 11 holes, and a few fish-scale shapes turned up too. Mapping with micro X-ray fluorescence found traces of cinnabar, a red mercury pigment, on nearly every scale tested. Some pieces carry flakes of a black coating, likely lacquer. The team found no gold or silver plating. A Han Dynasty iron suit from Linzi, which held 2,142 scales, was gilded.
Under a scanning electron microscope, five scales showed low-carbon steel, with 0.1 to 0.4 percent carbon. Grains measured 10 to 20 microns across, a sign of heavy hammering. Slag was scarce. Smiths most likely started with cast iron, stripped out carbon in a process called fining, and forged the result into thin sheets. This matches what researchers know about Qin iron work. The small sample leaves room for another route, direct smelting of solid iron.
The mausoleum holds other armor made of different materials. The Terracotta Army wears clay armor, and the brown scales seem to copy leather. Smaller gray scales on some higher-ranking figures might stand in for iron. In pit K9801, crews dug only about 1 percent of the area and pulled out 87 stone corselets and 43 stone helmets. Their scales look much like the M1 scales and were laced with flat copper wire.
Qin law texts written on bamboo slips hint at the cost. A penalty of making one set of scale armor equaled 168 to 224 days of labor. The authors say an iron suit, with smaller scales and finer lacing, might have kept a small workshop busy for a year or more.
One puzzle remains. Iron swords also lay in tomb M1, yet the mausoleum holds tens of thousands of bronze weapons. Some scholars think the bronze was symbolic. Old reign dates on weapons from Pit 1 suggest the army drew on aging stock. The authors don’t settle the debate. They plan to study more iron tools and weapons from the complex.

articles.title_orig: Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Before CEO Jensen Huang Testifies in Front of Congress on Dec. 1 and Dec. 3?
articles.title_zh: Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Before CEO Jensen Huang Testifies in Front of Congress on Dec. 1 and Dec. 3?
articles.content_orig:
By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 27, 2026 at 2:28PM EST
10 stocks we like better ›
Jensen Huang may be back as CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA +0.80% ) , but the chip giant's worries are far from over, as regulators and lawmakers continue to investigate whether Nvidia breached export controls and whether Huang's relationship with a Singaporean data center executive may have posed national security risks.
Huang and other Nvidia executives are set to testify before Congress next week on the above concerns, which the entire stock market will be watching.
On Dec. 1, Huang will testify before the U.S. House of Representatives' Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Committee, and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. Nvidia's General Counsel Tim Teter will also testify before the same committees on Dec. 2. Both hearings will be private, with transcripts not expected to be published publicly for some time.
But on Dec. 3, Huang will testify at a live hearing before the U.S. Senate Banking Committee, an event that will be closely monitored by all investors. Should investors buy Nvidia stock before these hearings?
While President Donald Trump has come out in support of Huang and claims to have played a role in his reinstatement, the hearings will help reveal how other lawmakers feel about Huang and what's going on with Nvidia.
"The market volatility and nervousness is centered on a number of issues that the Jensen soap opera has highlighted front and center," Yorkville Ives analyst and Managing Partner Dan Ives wrote in a recent research note, according to Business Insider. "Next week Jensen carries the weight of the entire tech sector and AI Revolution thesis when he marches into DC."
Huang's reinstatement as CEO led to a swift surge in the stock, but since then, shares have been pressured by lingering investor concerns about the company.
Multiple reports suggest that a woman Huang had an affair with, named Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at the Singaporean data center company MegaSpeed, may have facilitated a network that diverted advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese firms.
NASDAQ · As of 1:15 PM ET 11/27/26
Investors are trying to understand how much prior demand for Nvidia's chips, if any, may have been driven by similar sources. Since the scandal came to light, the U.S. Commerce Department has moved to close loopholes and tighten export controls that may have allowed Chinese firms to access Nvidia chips remotely.
The Commerce Department is now also requiring companies in select countries, such as Singapore and Indonesia, to obtain a license before transferring or reexporting advanced chips from U.S. companies.
In his note, Ives said he believes the impact on revenue resulting from such export controls is "a containable 15% to 20% at most." Still, that's a significant amount, and while some of it is priced in, Nvidia stock could certainly face more pressure if it believed future demand wouldn't be as strong.
Given that Wall Street analysts like Ives are already contemplating what would happen to Nvidia's revenue if increased export restrictions lower demand, or some sources of demand abroad are closed off, it's clear the market is pricing in at least some of the potential impact.
Still, Wall Street consensus estimates expect Nvidia to earn $16.61 per share on an adjusted basis for its fiscal year 2028 ending in late January 2028. That means Nvidia trades at just 9x forward earnings , so the valuation is attractive.
But as we've seen through this whole debacle, things can change in a hurry, so I would never tell investors to buy a stock based on a near-term event like a Congressional hearing.
With Nvidia trading at a cheap level, I think investors can purchase a position to hold long term. But I do not believe that the majority of a traditional stock portfolio should be concentrated in Nvidia or AI stocks, as much uncertainty remains.

articles.title_orig: U.S. Strikes Vessel Attempting Blockade Run Near Iran
articles.title_zh: U.S. Strikes Vessel Attempting Blockade Run Near Iran
articles.content_orig:
The military alleged the commercial vessel had "precision munitions."
Talks between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February. The opening strikes killed a host of top Iranian officials and commanders, among them Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway.
Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military, oil infrastructure and transport facilities.
See the most recent developments below.
U.S. Central Command said it disabled a commercial vessel with "precision munitions" in the Gulf of Oman Thursday after the ship allegedly tried to run the U.S. Naval blockade against Iran.
The U.S. military struck the ship's stern, disabling propulsion of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer shortly after it left an Iranian port, according to CENTCOM.
The military said that the ship's civilian crew was unharmed.
Gen. Sardar Shekarchi, spokesperson of Iran's armed forces, denies that Iran carried out a drone attack on Kuwait.
According to Iran's official state news agency IRNA, Shekarchi "categorically and completely" rejected claims by the Kuwaiti military that Iranian forces attacked vital Kuwaiti sites.
"No military or offensive operations have been conducted by the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran in the region," Shekarchi said, according to IRNA.
"Given the history of hostile actions -- including the use of 'false flag' tactics and regional adventurism by the Zionist regime and U.S. forces -- these accusations should be viewed as a cover for continued malevolence and an attempt to exacerbate insecurity in the region," Shekarchi said.
Kuwaiti authorities have blamed Iran for the attack that killed two Italian nationals and injured one Kuwaiti and one Pakistani national.
-ABC News' Jamie Dorrington
The two Italian nationals injured in Thursday's Iranian drone attack in Kuwait have died, a spokesperson for Kuwait's Ministry of Defense said in a statement.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed her condolences to the victim's families in a post on X.
"On behalf of myself and the Government, I express my deepest sorrow and extend my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families. My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families," Meloni said.
The Kuwait Army on Thursday reported that four people were injured by falling shrapnel after an Iranian drone attack targeted "a vital site" in the Gulf state.
The army said in a post to X that Kuwaiti forces "dealt with" the incoming drones. "Material damage also occurred," the statement added.
Those injured were two Italian nationals, one Pakistani national and one Kuwaiti national, the army said.

According to U.S. Central Command, a tanker ship attempting to run the naval Iran blockade was disabled after its crew refused to listen to multiple warnings.
A U.S. military aircraft disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after it tried to evade the naval blockade of all Iranian ports, which has been in effect since mid-July.
The Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer left Bandar Abbas, a major port city on Iran's southern coast, before the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) fired precision munitions at the ship's stern, destroying its propulsion.
A video released by the military shows a projectile hitting the back of the ship and causing an explosion. The civilian crew was unharmed in the strike, CENTCOM said.
So far, U.S. forces have redirected 158 compliant commercial vessels and disabled six that refused to comply.
The moment a U.S. military aircraft struck a Palau-flagged commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman on Nov. 26, 2026. The ship left Bandar Abbas and tried to slip through the U.S. naval blockade. (U.S. Central Command)

President Donald Trump said Thursday, while celebrating Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, that victory in the Iran war would come "whenever I want it."
"We have victory at hand. It's going to be whenever, sort of, whatever I want it to be. To be honest, and we're trying to be nice, we're giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that," he said in a phone call to U.S. service members.
Trump also praised U.S. troops for their role in preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.
President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump speak with participate in calls with U.S. service members from Mar-a-Lago on Thanksgiving Day, on Nov. 26, 2026 in Palm Beach, Florida. (Daniel Heuer/Getty Images)

"Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They will never have a nuclear weapon. That I can tell you," he said.
Trump added that the U.S. has launched 150 missiles to intercept threats targeting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz .
Asked whether Moscow and Beijing are providing Iran with intelligence to help it target U.S. military bases, Trump minimized the likelihood and said China was not heavily involved. He maintained that both countries are interested in helping the U.S. bring the war to a close.

articles.title_orig: China is making inroads into Europe’s skies with cheap plane fuel. Brussels takes aim
articles.title_zh: China is making inroads into Europe’s skies with cheap plane fuel. Brussels takes aim
articles.content_orig:
Not all green fuel comes with a green light / Photo: Pexels
Cheap green fuel from abroad could help Europe clean up its skies, but it may also ground the continent’s own producers. Brussels is now launching an anti-dumping investigation into imports from China and Singapore, amid claims that low-priced Asian competition is squeezing European manufacturers out of the market.
The EU wants more sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) in its aircraft tanks. But cheap imports from Asia could undermine the European industry it hopes to build.
The European Commission has therefore launched an anti-dumping investigation into SAF imports from China and Singapore. The probe will examine not only the price of the finished fuel, but also the conditions under which Chinese producers obtain a key raw material.
The European Biodiesel Board (EBB) filed the complaint on 15 October on behalf of European sustainable aviation fuel producers. It argues that imports from both Asian countries are growing and capturing an increasing share of the EU market.
Their rising volumes and low prices are putting pressure on European producers’ sales. According to the complaint, this is taking a toll on their overall performance and financial health.
In a notice published in the Official Journal, the Commission said the evidence submitted was sufficient to justify opening an investigation. This does not yet mean dumping has been established. The investigation must determine whether it is actually taking place.
One particularly interesting aspect of the complaint concerns China’s market for raw materials. SAF producers use, among other things, used cooking oil (UCO). According to the document, it accounts for around 70 per cent of the fuel’s production costs.
The EBB claims that UCO prices in China are significantly lower than those on comparable international markets.
The government also intervenes in how the raw material is exported. “According to the evidence in the complaint, used cooking oil (…) is not subject to VAT rebate on exports from the People’s Republic of China,” the Commission’s notice states.
This keeps a key feedstock on the domestic market, allowing China to focus on producing and exporting a higher-value product. The Commission will examine whether these conditions distort feedstock prices and give Chinese producers an unfair competitive advantage.
The investigation into China will also look at wider state intervention in the economy. The complaint points to the influence of China’s financial system, land market and labour conditions on fuel production and sales.
It argues that domestic prices and costs cannot provide a reliable basis for comparison. Instead, it proposes using Thailand as a reference country when calculating the product’s normal value.
The approach to Singapore is different. The Commission lacks reliable data on domestic prices there. It will therefore calculate normal value using production costs, administrative and selling expenses, and profit.
Sustainable aviation fuel is one way to reduce aviation’s carbon footprint . Unlike conventional kerosene, it comes from renewable feedstocks or waste streams. It can also be used without completely overhauling existing aircraft or aviation infrastructure.
That makes SAF a key part of the EU’s plans to green air transport. The ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation gradually raises the minimum share of sustainable fuels that aviation fuel suppliers must provide at EU airports.
The requirement started at two per cent in 2025. It will rise to six per cent in 2030 and 70 per cent by 2050.
As mandatory demand grows, new producers and investment in European production capacity have an opportunity to emerge. But competing against fuel made at significantly lower costs could make life harder for European companies.
This creates an awkward contradiction. Cheaper imports can help meet rising demand for low-carbon fuel. At the same time, they could weaken the domestic industry expected to sustain the transition in the long run.
The anti-dumping investigation will establish whether SAF enters the EU at prices below its normal value. It will also assess whether this causes injury to European producers.
If the allegations are confirmed, the Commission could impose additional duties on imports from the countries concerned. But this is not automatic. It must establish dumping, injury to the European industry and a causal link between the two.
The Commission also plans to register imports of SAF from China and Singapore from the early stages of the investigation. This matters for importers, too. “This may lead to retroactive collection of definitive duties on registered imports,” the Commission warns.
The investigation must conclude within 14 months of the notice’s publication. The Commission could introduce provisional duties after around seven to eight months.

articles.content_orig:
SpaceX shares rose 4.83% in Friday's shortened trading session, amid broader Nasdaq gains and after CEO Elon Musk expanded his SpaceX share-donation plan for U.S. children.
Other tech-related stocks, including Micron , Qualcomm , Lumentum and Tesla all gained over 5% on Friday as the sector rebounded from a heavy sell-off earlier this week. SanDisk was Friday's biggest mover as investors rotated back into some AI trade names , surging 15.96%.
Musk posted on X on Thursday, "I will be donating another share of SpaceX to all kids in America every year."
After Musk's post, SpaceX shares jumped more than 7% in overnight trading on Blue Ocean ATS, an alternative trading system for U.S. equities that runs during the nighttime hours. U.S. stock exchanges were closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday and closed at 1 p.m. ET on Friday.
Shares closed 1.30% higher on Wednesday ahead of Thanksgiving.
The latest pledge follows SpaceX's announcement Wednesday that it would donate one share of its Class A stock to all active Trump Accounts, tax-advantaged investment accounts for American children, with Musk personally matching the gift.
In a separate post on X, Musk said SpaceX's contribution would be transferred next month, while his personal donation would follow when his lockup period expires in June next year.
Nearly 70 million Trump Accounts had been created as of October, according to the White House.
Since the program's launch in July, families and friends have contributed more than $1 billion to the accounts, bringing total deposits from all sources to more than $9 billion, CNBC reported earlier this week.
The FCC also announced Wednesday that it granted SpaceX approval to deploy 1 million data center satellites for the company's Starmind constellation.
Speaking on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Friday, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said the authorization of SpaceX's satellites will have ripple effects within the industry as well.
"Not just SpaceX, but all sorts of different players in this market. Because at the end of the day, we want everyone to compete and succeed. I think we're going to see a lot of players entering this space soon," Carr said.

articles.title_orig: Spanish Police Find a Vast Marijuana Bunker Beneath a Backyard Playground
articles.title_zh: Spanish Police Find a Vast Marijuana Bunker Beneath a Backyard Playground
articles.content_orig:
By Molly Grace •
                                            Published: 26 Nov 2026 • 21:54                                                                • 2 minutes read
Officers lifted the artificial grass and found an access hatch. Photo credit: Guardia Civil/Ministro de Interior
A children’s playground is supposed to be somewhere parents can let their little ones run around without a second thought. But in Granada, the swings, playhouse and artificial grass were hiding something far more sinister: a concealed entrance to an underground cannabis farm containing 1,954 plants.
The underground plantation was found on a property in Las Gabias, where the Guardia Civil uncovered the entrance beneath what appeared to be a small children’s playground. The surface had been dressed with artificial grass, a swing, a playhouse and a small mat. White decorative stone covered the surrounding ground, helping disguise the structure. It was not simply a cannabis farm hidden in a basement. The play area itself concealed a hydraulic hatch and a vehicle ramp leading down into the bunker.
Officers lifted the artificial grass and found an access hatch used to operate a large hydraulic door. Once it was opened, a ramp led down into the underground installation, which measured around 180 square metres and stood five metres high. Inside around 2,000 cannabis plants in two large growing rooms. Both were fitted with lighting, ventilation and climate-control systems designed to support intensive cultivation.
The discovery raises an obvious question about the setting: the entrance had been disguised as a place for children to play. The Guardia Civil has not said that children were present or that the area was being used by children, but the equipment was deliberately arranged to make the concealed access look like an ordinary play space.
Investigators also found an electricity tower which was allegedly being used to make an illegal connection to the power network. The load detected was equivalent to the electricity consumption of around 100 homes.
The bunker was described by the Guardia Civil as the largest and most sophisticated underground cannabis-growing installation discovered so far in Granada province.
The discovery formed part of Operation Nazarí-Sabika 04, an investigation into an alleged criminal organisation involved in growing and processing cannabis and supplying specialist equipment to other drug-trafficking groups across Spain. The operation began more than a year ago and entered its main phase on November 17, when officers carried out 13 searches in Granada city and the municipalities of Albolote, Jun, Las Gabias and Maracena.
Five people were arrested and three others are being investigated on suspicion of drug cultivation and production, electricity fraud, illegal possession of a prohibited weapon and membership of a criminal group. The alleged ringleader has been remanded in custody. Across the three plantations uncovered during the searches, officers seized 2,479 cannabis plants. They also confiscated two cars, two vans, a caravan, a trailer, a stun gun and €22,970 in cash.
Officers also sealed premises specialising in cannabis-growing equipment, known as a grow shop, which was allegedly linked to the organisation. The Guardia Civil estimates its value at several million euros. Investigators believe the shop’s owner used it to obtain equipment for the underground plantation and to supply products to other locations around Spain.
The investigation was carried out by the Guardia Civil’s criminal intelligence and Policía Judicial units in Granada, together with officers from its Las Gabias investigation team.

articles.title_orig: Spain’s Pedro Sanchez bets on left-wing voting surge to defy election polls
articles.title_zh: Spain’s Pedro Sanchez bets on left-wing voting surge to defy election polls
articles.content_orig:
Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez appears sure he will secure a left-wing majority in ⁠a snap general election on Sunday, despite adverse public polling suggesting a right-wing advantage.
“I can’t conceive of us losing,” the Socialist leader told radio station SER on Friday, as political parties prepared to wrap up campaigning before the vote.
The outcome of the election will be closely watched as Europe opens an electoral cycle over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the European Union.
Amid a legal ban on publishing opinion surveys within five days of an election, Sanchez ⁠insisted that internal data suggested his Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party (PSOE) would win the most votes, allowing him to clinch re-election with the support of smaller leftist allies.
He said that left-leaning voters were increasingly mobilising to turn out in droves, a prerequisite for reaching ‌a progressive majority to tackle issues such as the country’s deep housing crisis.
However, nearly all the polls released before the ban showed a clear advantage for a potential coalition between the conservative People’s Party (PP) and far-right Vox, which seek to oust Sanchez after eight years in power.
Earlier, during a televised pre-election debate, Sanchez clashed with PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo and Vox’s Santiago Abascal, as well as Ada Colau, a left-wing Spanish politician and former mayor of Barcelona associated with the Sumar political alliance, in a debate focused on immigration, the housing crisis and foreign policy.
The prime minister criticised the Madrid regional government, controlled by the PP, for awarding an honorary medal to the Israeli government while the assault on Gaza continued.
“It is shameful,” Sanchez said, accusing his opponents of having “no humanity whatsoever.”
He also interrupted Feijoo when the conservative leader described Israel’s actions in Gaza as a “massacre”, insisting that “it is genocide”.
Sanchez warned voters that Spain faced a choice between “regression and progressivism”, arguing that the PP and Vox wanted to replicate the politics of US President Donald Trump and Argentinian President Javier Milei.
Sanchez has vaunted his record on the international stage, notably his outspoken defence of immigration, clashes with Trump and criticism of Israel. The dynamism of the EU’s fourth-largest economy under his leadership has also drawn praise at a turbulent time for global markets.
But a polarising status at home puts his tenure in peril.
Sanchez is holding his final large rally in Madrid on Friday, seeking a late mobilisation of left-wing voters to defeat what he calls the “regression” of a possible PP-Vox coalition.
“We are unstoppable and we will win!” he told a Socialist meeting in the western city of Plasencia, sporting a red T-shirt emblazoned with the slogan “the power of women”.
He contrasted a Spain “of prosperity, principles and values” against a “reactionary coalition” that would question women’s rights, cut pensions and gut public services.
PP leader Feijoo, who won the most seats at the last election in 2023 but failed to form a government, told supporters in Barcelona: “This time we will pull it off.”
Dismissing Sanchez’s campaign of “fear”, he will hold his campaign finale in Seville, capital of the southern Andalusia region.
Addressing reporters before a closing rally in the eastern city of Valencia, Vox leader Abascal accused Sanchez’s “mafia-style” government of “betraying, robbing and lying” to the country.
Spaniards will observe a “day of reflection” on the ‌eve ‌of the vote on Saturday. Campaigning, rallies and political advertising are banned so voters can weigh their choices before heading to the polls.

articles.title_orig: ‘GTA 6’ Is Already One Of The Best-Selling Games Ever, Report Says
articles.title_zh: ‘GTA 6’ Is Already One Of The Best-Selling Games Ever, Report Says
articles.content_orig:
It is technically perfect in its rendition of imperfection, evocative in a way that can’t be explained and must be experienced. And it can be experienced on many different levels.
It is technically perfect in its rendition of imperfection, evocative in a way that can’t be explained and must be experienced. And it can be experienced on many different levels.
Grand Theft Auto VI , the sprawling new video game released last week by Rockstar Games , is the latest edition of the most lucrative media franchise on Earth. How lucrative? It made an estimated $3.8 billion on its first day . That’s bigger than the Avengers. It’s bigger than Harry Potter and the Transphobic Author . It’s bigger than the Super Bowl. It’s the biggest single thing in culture right now. And that appears to be confusing a lot of people who don’t play video games. For the uninitiated, GTA is essentially a sandbox crime simulator. It allows you to steal cars, sell drugs, and run over pedestrians as you flee from the cops you haven’t yet shot. It allows you to stick up a Waffle House, drag an ATM through the streets until it breaks open, and murder every civilian in an only lightly fictionalized rendition of the state of Florida.
The fact that this is the most popular thing on the planet seems to be scrambling many brains. I keep seeing the same question from non-gamers: Why ? Why has this video game broken containment and landed in the center of American and even global public discourse? Why does it make so much money? Why is it everywhere ?
I feel like I am well situated to answer these questions, because, while I’m a normal American dad with a wife and children and a full-time job and all the other indicia of normal adult responsibility, I’m also an avid gamer. Most people who play video games will buy only one or two a year ; I probably buy a new game (often on sale) every six to eight weeks. I generally find at least 10 hours a week to play them—though really, the weeks when I only play 10 hours are, like, “election week” or “a week when a hurricane knocked out my power for days.”
So, with my bona fides out of the way: the first thing I tell non-gamers about GTA , or any video game, is that “it’s art.” Thinking about GTA as art helps to explain everything else that’s happening around it, because GTA is the Mona Lisa of this art form. It is technically perfect in its rendition of imperfection. It is evocative in a way that can’t be explained and must be experienced. And it can be experienced on many different levels. Some people want to see the Mona Lisa just to say that they’ve seen it. Some people will see it and not get what all the fuss is about (the French call those people “Americans”). Some people will see it and feel moved to their core. The same thing happens with GTA : It has a fairly linear “Bonnie and Clyde” type of story with a couple of different endings, but no two people will experience GTA in exactly the same way.
Of course, the Mona Lisa isn’t going to pull out a gun and start shooting paintballs at the other portraits. Nor is she going to remove her top and start shaking her money-maker. So let’s get into that. Yes, GTA is violent and hypersexualized. There is a lot of shooting, there are a lot of boobs and penises, and all the violence and sex is delivered with a steady stream of foul language and crude humor. If you want to be mad at the game, the game will give you something to be mad about, no matter your politics. Indeed, right now the people who are most mad at the game are the white-wing manosphere. The game tracks the relationship between the two main characters (who are in a cis-heteronormative relationship) and essentially encourages you to be a “good boyfriend/girlfriend.” The notion of being nice to a woman has made the manosphere lose its mind. Oh no, the game gives you the option to buy flowers for your girlfriend as part of a quest! Men are doomed! You can also not buy her flowers, or you can, I assume, murder the flower-shop guy and take the flowers (but I didn’t try to do that because I am a normal freaking person whose masculinity is not threatened by showing affection).
Just like the sex—or, in the case of the manosphere, the “acknowledging that a woman is a human being”— the violence in GTA is going to turn a lot of people off. But here’s the thing I think most non-gamers do not understand: GTA isn’t the most violent video game on the market. It’s not in the top 10 violent video games that are broadly popular right now. I wouldn’t even rank GTA VI as the most violent video game I’ve played this year . It’s also not the most sexually explicit game I’ve played recently: Baldur’s Gate 3 (a role-playing game that won Game of the Year in 2023) allows you to play with your characters fully nude, if you want to. It famously lets you have sex with a bear.
GTA is not popular because of the violence or sex. The thing that makes GTA popular is the agency you have over the violence. Yes, you can run over pedestrians, but you can also not do that. You can shoot all the cops in the head as you blast your way out of a bank with cash stuffed in the duffel bag, or you can carefully plan your heist so that you trip no alarms and get away without firing a shot. You can’t play the game as a pacifist (you are a criminal; you will be committing crimes; the authorities will try to stop you from committing crimes; this will often lead to violence), but your ultimate body count is your own and reflects your choices, not the game’s.
It’s that agency that makes GTA a totally different experience from other games that are facially far more violent and bloody. If you put me in an average mission in the popular first-person shooter Call of Duty , I’m going to kill a lot of people. The game will call those people “terrorists” because I’m not supposed to feel bad about killing them, but it will give me no success condition other than murdering every terrorist in the compound. In GTA , by comparison, there was an early mission where my friend was kidnapped by odious redneck pig farmers. They were coded as rednecks so that a certain type of person (namely me) wouldn’t feel bad should violence become necessary. Once I freed him, the game gave me the option of
I went with option 3. GTA is popular not because option 3 exists—option 3 exists in pretty much every video game. GTA is popular because options 1 and 2 also exist , so when you choose option 3 you feel it . It makes the killing more of a personal choice than a gameplay mechanic. Most games allow you to kill; GTA is a success because you don’t have to.
Choice and consequence over murder or mercy is not unique to GTA . In fact, I’ve played a lot of games with far more difficult and engaging murder choices than “kill rednecks, yes/no?” But what makes GTA truly special, and a cultural phenomenon rather than simply a very good video game, is that it is a satirical take on us: America in the 2020s. The game is not set in medieval Europe. There are no dragons or witches. It is set in only lightly fictionalized Florida. If you walk down the street in the GTA ’s main city (called “Vice City”), you will feel like you’re walking around Miami.
The game cost well over a billion dollars and 13 years to make, and part of that budget went toward sending game developers to Miami and around Florida to just watch, observe, and report back. It’s reactive in a way never before seen: Random characters will be having random conversations that don’t involve you, and react as one might expect them to if you pull a gun on them: most will run; some will fight; some will just shrug and be like “joke’s on you, I’m broke.”
You will see every body type, fashion choice, race, color, or creed in the game that you might see on any street in America. You’ll hear music blaring out of certain stores. You’ll see car accidents that don’t involve the player at all. One random character tried to steal my car (it didn’t work out well for him).

In an address to slighted Xbox customers, Playtonic explains why a new "Yooka-Laylee" edition is not coming to Xbox Series X |S.
Banjo-Kazooie is one of Xbox's most-requested, and most-dormant franchises, with fans of a certain age awash with nostalgia for early 00s 3D platformers. The genre hasn't exactly remained popular in recent years, but PlayStation's Astrobot has more than proven that there's still juice to be squeezed if the game is positioned properly.
Playtonic took up the Banjo mantle with its spiritual successor, Yooka-Laylee, featuring a superficially similar duo inspired by Rare's golden era.
Given Microsoft's ownership of the Banjo IP, you might expect Yooka-Laylee to have a decent chunk of fans and players on Xbox, but Playtonic says that they're not enough to justify this latest port.
Hi everyone, please read the following regarding the situation for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition on Xbox Series S/X - https://t.co/IQeesCczo6 November 27, 2026
In a statement on social media, Playtonic says "Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure," describing the new version complete with visual upgrades and other new content. "Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," indirectly referring to Xbox, which isn't getting this new edition.
"We understand the frustration felt by those of you who won't be able to access the Definitive Edition at launch, but unfortunately the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time. As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this."
Game journalist Chris Dring chimed in and suggested that developers are findng it "harder to financially justify" launching on Xbox.
Over the last 18 months, a few devs have told that it's proving harder to financially justify launching on Xbox.
However, GTA 6 has done around 10m on Xbox now. That's a lot of people who have turned on the machine! Could be an opportunity. November 27, 2026
It's certainly true that Xbox is the smallest of the big three platforms by userbase, and purchasing habits are likely skewed due to Xbox Game Pass on top. However, many, many indie developers release on Xbox without an Xbox Game Pass deal and find success regardless. Many of these developers consistently launch games into Xbox Play Anywhere to take advantage of the platform beyond Xbox Series X|S consoles too across PC and cloud, with more than half of games launching with Xbox Play Anywhere per monthly average.
Microsoft has historically been very friendly towards indie developers in recent years, paying out literally billions of dollars via the ID@Xbox program . It may have seen some de-emphasis in recent months however, with new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma taking the reins.
Whether or not we'll eventually see Yooka-Laylee on Xbox remains to be seen, but at least for now, users are stuck with the older versions of the game for the foreseeable.

articles.title_orig: Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea Of Sorrow DLC Finally Has A Release Date
articles.title_zh: Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea Of Sorrow DLC Finally Has A Release Date
articles.content_orig:
Heya Gang. It’s Cherry Time!
We’ve just announced three exciting new games being developed by a few of our close friends, and, if that wasn’t enough, there’s now an imminent release date for Hollow Knight: Silksong’s first big content update - Sea of Sorrow! Arriving free for all players on December 11!
You can check out the full presentation right here:
In Sea of Sorrow, players will voyage above and beneath Pharloom’s forgotten ocean, across islands, through forts and into deep caverns beneath the waves. We’ve spent the whole year stuffing this adventure full with all the things you’d expect from Hollow Knight: Silksong - crazed characters, high adventure, and epic bosses! It’s also overflowing with more exceptional music by the eternally talented Christopher Larkin! We’re pretty darn excited to get it into all of your hands on December 11, so please look forward to it.
While we’ve been busy on the vast oceans of the Undersea, our friends Rohan, Lukas and Makoto have been hard at work bringing their own worlds to life, each with its own impressive scope and style. We’d happily speak at length about their talents, but why hear more from us when you can hear directly from the creators themselves? Watch the short docos below and let them introduce you to their games, their inspirations, and their beginnings.
As soon as their games are ready, these new titles will be releasing under the brand new Team Cherry Presents label. But what have we busy cherry-folk got to do with these titles, you ask? We’ll we’re glad you did, because Team Cherry had a hand in each game through our fourth and newest member, Huy Le!
Officially Huy acts as the technical director and on-going support for all the Team Cherry Presents games, building robust foundations, bespoke creation tools, puzzle mechanics, and solving countless issues for each developer as they arise. But Huy’s also become something of a secret weapon on the Cherry side, tagging in to assist on Silksong (and now Sea of Sorrow) during the intensive lead-ups to launch. Initially that meant taking on some of Silksong’s many ports, but ultimately it’s included much more - such as resolving countless bugs and implementing integral features (Autosaves, Achievements, HD rumble!).
As a long-time team of three people, adding a fourth member is a big deal! So please everyone welcome Huy to the unit and to Team Cherry Presents.
And finally, a physical news drop! Just last week, our friends at Fangamer unveiled a whole bunch of adorable new Hollow Knight: Silksong merch. They’ve revealed pins, posters, plush and more! A big thank you to them for their continued passion for the world of Hollow Knight, and an extra big thanks for creating the cutest, softest singing-Sherma around.
fangamer.com Worldwide, fangamer.eu UK & EU, fangamer.jp Japan
That’s a wrap on Cherry Time! Watch those stylish docos! Jump over and wishlist the new games on Steam! We’ll be sharing more details about these games soon, and on our own ever-ambitious plans, but for now Sea of Sorrow is imminent and Team Cherry has to start prepping!
